relations: High, low and exit center heights are fixed; each roof/bank pair derives from one shared aperture
Roof and bank horizontal runs are unequal, offset and overlapping, not repeated paired pipes

Extended inserts180px inside the existing high shelf and translates only the suffix; duration gains1.2s
limitations: Disjoint static bands require a height change, not the exact larger illustrated wave
No native trajectory, input range, camera readability, seam or human-play claim
The earlier v1 flat-y270 counterexample remains valid for v1; this uses its corrected successor

relations.spring_to_receiver: gate center=top−R−.01−b²/(2g)+offset; gate front time=t_reference+.85*b/g; both use a conditional top reset, not an observed event
relations.whole_width: hold extends from front−.08 to whole-radius tail+.12; width+2R is included, not only center crossing
relations.not_arrival_triggered: gate clock is fixed from authored reference; actual spring contact may be earlier/later/absent. No clock reset, no wait.
relations.reference_scope: closed-form constant-gravity quantities are layout estimates, not native discrete trajectories or input feasibility; support bands at expanded front/tail are conservative near corners
relations.native_spring: default contact: any circle/body hit can trigger; oldY<spring.y+h/2 chooses top. No descending-only filter or timed-course substitution.
relations.order: flap sets vy−290 at tick start; a later spring collision in that tick can override it. A flap on a later tick can override the bounce.
relations.cooldown: per source, tick+ceil(.35/DT); active body remains and contact is not automatically retriggered while cooldown is running

provider_metadata.optional_bypass: Flap above the spring and enter the same aperture with ordinary cadence. Spring avoidance is legitimate and changes preparation/input history; no claim it is harder or worse until compared. There is no outside bypass around the full-height gate.

test_question.goal: Can an actual top-contact tape retain the stronger reset, then catch with a later flap through the entire gate and recover? Compare a post-contact early flap and an avoid-spring tape.
measure: actual first bounce tick, side, x/y/vy and cooldown
flap times and actual exit state
test_question.early_flap_limit: Only compare after a real bounce and record the next-tick flap. Same-tick input can be overwritten by contact; later flaps may be necessary. Never interpret no-early-flap as no-flap forever.
test_question.controller_sketch: Observe first actual top bounce; compare retain versus next-tick flap, then use the same declared downstream feedback. An avoidance tape is a separate branch, not a forged no-bounce checkpoint.

preview_contract.rule: spring and aperture silhouettes appear during approach; do not invent contact-triggered opening cues

risks: actual top contact may not happen at reference x/time
side or bottom contact uses oldY midpoint and can push downward
retaining bounce too long can fall into lower gate; an early or late flap may still work under other input histories
cooldown collision can overlap active spring without a new reset; body is not removed
full-open clock coverage does not prove y/vy passage
spring avoidance may be cheaper; compare before claiming gameplay value

limitations: Bounce speed must be positive and satisfy coupled author constraints. Reference contact and continuous gravity arc remain hypothetical.
Default two-sided oldY spring, snap/body/cooldown and full gate clock persist. No mandatory contact or native impulse is inferred from generation.
A late-gate author-rule rejection may still leave a partial aperture; it is not all-route impossibility.

relations: Q-in closing begins exactly when Q-out opening begins
Q-out closing begins exactly when A-in opening begins; no per-body clock reset
